question.worked_solution:
To evaluate this expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, consider the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\times (-5)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Applying PEMDAS to this expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\times (-5)^{2} & = \\ 3\times 25 & = \\ 75\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{aligned}(3\times (-5)^{2})÷\frac{5}{2} & = \\ 75÷\frac{5}{2} & = \\ 75\times \frac{2}{5} & = \\ \frac{75}{1}\times \frac{2}{5} & = \\ \frac{75\times 2}{1\times 5} & = \\ \frac{150}{5} & = \\ 30\end{aligned}
$$
